body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert PD-7421 fired for service=redis-prod cluster=prod-redis-01 metric=redis_maxclients > 90%

pagerduty: PD-7421 - incident triggered by redis_maxclients on prod-redis-01 - unacked

Aditi (oncall): Acked. I’m on it. Paging SRE and DB.

Miguel (sre): Oncall looking. Is PG also affected or just Redis? Any 5xx from API?

Aditi (oncall): App errors spiked ~08:12 UTC. Frontend reports connection/timeouts to embed-generation endpoints. Error rate ~4.8% now. Short spike in tail latencies.

Dana (db-engineer): Seeing both redis maxclients and high waiters on pgbouncer for the generation DB. Likely client saturation cascade (clients pool to DB via queue).

Aditi (oncall): Running quick checks.

cli-bot: ```
$ redis-cli -h prod-redis-01 INFO clients | egrep "connected_clients|blocked_clients"
connected_clients:512
blocked_clients:14
# maxclients configured at 550
```

Aditi (oncall): `connected_clients=512` and bursts up to 540 in last 5m. close to max.

Dana (db-engineer): pgbouncer shows many waiters. ```
$ psql -h pgbouncer-host -c "SHOW POOLS;"
database | cl_active | cl_waiting | sv_active | sv_idle
gen_db  |   120     |   95       |    40    |   6
```
cl_waiting=95 is terrible.

Miguel (sre): Likely a worker job or customer job fan-out caused an explosion. Need short-term mitigation: 1) throttle ingress at API gateway for downstream generation routes 2) increase pgbouncer pool and allow more db connections (if capacity) 3) identify offending client host(s) and cordon.

Aditi (oncall): Kicking off API rate-limit rule now (temporarily drop large requests to /v1/generate). Applying policy to tenant-heavy routes.

Aditi (oncall): Applied temporary 10rps soft-limit for generation routes for unknown tenants. :white_check_mark:

Miguel (sre): Increasing pgbouncer pool by +50 to relieve waiters. Dana, is DB CPU/memory safe if we let a few more connections?

Dana (db-engineer): We can bump pgbouncer pool to allow more clients (up to +80) but only short-term. DB CPU currently 65% — safe to absorb some more connections for ~30min. I'll apply +60.

Dana (db-engineer): ```
# update pgbouncer config (applied)
max_client_conn = 10000
default_pool_size = 20 -> 30
```

Aditi (oncall): Also checking Redis client list for repeat offenders. Running `CLIENT LIST`.

cli-bot: ```
$ redis-cli -h prod-redis-01 CLIENT LIST | head -n 6
id=2325 addr=10.2.14.9:42311 fd=7 name=worker-109 age=120 idle=0 flags=N db=0 sub=0 psub=0 multi=-1 qbuf=0 qbuf-free=0 obl=0 oll=0 omem=0 events=r cmd=get
id=2330 addr=10.2.14.9:42312 fd=8 name=worker-110 age=118 idle=0 flags=N db=0 ...
id=5001 addr=52.34.11.2:33421 fd=12 name=api-gw rate-limit=none
...
```

Aditi (oncall): Seeing dozens of connections from 10.2.14.9 with worker-* names. Looks like a batch fanout.

Miguel (sre): If that's a job runner, we should pause or stagger the job. Can we identify release or cron? @deploy-team?

Dana (db-engineer): For immediate relief, we can kill some idle worker connections to free slots. I can target the worst offenders.

Aditi (oncall): Go ahead Dana. Meanwhile keep the API throttle on and notify customers with high request volumes.

Dana (db-engineer): Killing 40 worker connections now. ```
$ redis-cli -h prod-redis-01 CLIENT KILL addr 10.2.14.9:42311
KILLED
```

Aditi (oncall): After kills: connected_clients down to 430. pgbouncer waiters dropped to ~22. Error rate fell to 1.2%.

Miguel (sre): Nice. Keep throttles until we confirm full recovery. Also recommend enabling short-lived retry/backoff in clients and moving heavy jobs to batched windows.

Aditi (oncall): I’m going to hand off paging. I need to grab a quick meeting. Miguel, you take incident lead?

Miguel (sre): I’m on it. Taking lead at 3187654350. Will coordinate with DB and deploy team for root cause.

pagerduty: PD-7421 - acknowledged by Aditi, reassigned to Miguel.

Dana (db-engineer): Follow-up immediate remediation: increase pgbouncer pool permanently from 20->30 for the next 72h, add a connection filter for worker hosts, and create a dashboard alert for sudden client IP concentration.

Miguel (sre): Also creating a short blocking rule in the rate-limiter to protect redis and db for the next 60 minutes if spikes reappear.

Aditi (oncall): Customer impact: generation endpoints saw elevated latencies and 4.8% errors at peak for ~6 minutes. Affected tenants: pool-heavy customers and some self-hosted pipelines. No data loss. Recording incident severity as P1->P2 downscale after stabilization.

Miguel (sre): Logging action items:
- ACTION-1: (Dana) Add connection-level filter to drop/slow requests from worker IPs if over X conns (dued 3h)
- ACTION-2: (Platform) Add tenant-level soft limits and sticky rate-limiting for generation endpoints (dued 6h)
- ACTION-3: (Infra) Add alert: sudden >20% of redis clients from single IP (dued 12h)
- ACTION-4: (SRE) Postmortem and capacity plan for pgbouncer/db and redis (dued 48h)

Dana (db-engineer): Filed follow-up ticket INC-789 in tracker with initial notes.

Miguel (sre): Marking incident mitigated for now. Keep throttles on for 30m and monitor. If error rate <0.5% and waiters <10 we close.

Aditi (oncall): :white_check_mark: I hand back to Miguel. Thanks.

cli-bot: ```:info: metrics snapshot: redis_connected=428 redis_maxclients_pct=77% pgbouncer_waiters=9 api_error_rate=0.4%```

pagerduty: PD-7421 - resolved (manual) by Miguel at 3187654380

Miguel (sre): Closing notes: no persistent corruption, root cause appears to be a simultaneous job fan-out from internal worker fleet. Postmortem will include who triggered the job window and recommended gating.

Dana (db-engineer): Will also add a runbook entry for 'kill noisy redis clients' and safe pgbouncer bump steps.

Aditi (oncall): Filed short customer notification draft for CS to send to affected tenants.

Miguel (sre): Good work team. Follow-ups assigned. :thumbsup:
